title: Why the Moon Changes Shape
learning_objectives: Learn that the Moon does not make its own light and that we see the sunlit part
Name the four main Moon phases in order

factual_claims.claim: The Moon does not make its own light; it reflects light from the Sun.
factual_claims.source: NASA Space Place, 'What are the Moon's phases?' (spaceplace.nasa.gov/moon-phases)

factual_claims.claim: The Moon travels around the Earth about once a month.
factual_claims.source: NASA Science, 'Moon Phases' (science.nasa.gov/moon/moon-phases) - one orbit takes about 27 days; the phase cycle about 29.5 days

factual_claims.claim: We see different amounts of the Moon's lit half as it moves around Earth, which is why its shape seems to change.
factual_claims.source: NASA Space Place, 'What are the Moon's phases?'

factual_claims.claim: The main phases in order are new moon, first quarter (half), full moon, last quarter (half).
The whole Moon is always there, even when we can only see a thin part of it.
factual_claims.source: NASA Space Place, 'What are the Moon's phases?'

parent_prompts: Before: what shape was the Moon last night? Does it always look like that?
Try it: in a dark room, shine a torch (the Sun) on a ball (the Moon) and walk the ball around the child's head (the Earth).
After: is part of the Moon really missing when it looks thin?

pages.text: Some nights the Moon is a round white plate. Some nights it is a thin curved slice. Does the Moon really change shape?
pages.illustration_brief: Night sky split in two: a full round Moon on the left, a thin crescent on the right.
pages.audio_script: Some nights the Moon is a round white plate. Some nights it is a thin curved slice. Does the Moon really change shape?
pages.image_alt: Night sky split in two: a full round Moon on the left, a thin crescent on the right.

pages.text: No. The Moon is always a whole ball. What changes is how much of it we can see lit up.
pages.illustration_brief: A grey ball (Moon) with one half brightly lit, the other half in shadow.
pages.audio_script: No. The Moon is always a whole ball. What changes is how much of it we can see lit up.
pages.image_alt: A grey ball with one half brightly lit, the other half in shadow.

pages.text: The Moon makes no light of its own. It shines because sunlight bounces off it, the way a mirror shines when you hold it in the sun.
pages.illustration_brief: The Sun on the left, light rays hitting the Moon, bouncing toward a small Earth.
pages.audio_script: The Moon makes no light of its own. It shines because sunlight bounces off it, the way a mirror shines when you hold it in the sun.

vocabulary.definition: Bounces light back instead of making it.

pages.image_alt: The Sun on the left, light rays hitting the Moon, bouncing toward a small Earth.

pages.text: The Moon travels around the Earth. One trip takes about a month. As it moves, we see its sunny side from different angles.
pages.illustration_brief: Diagram: Earth in the centre, the Moon at several positions on a circle around it, the Sun far to one side.
pages.audio_script: The Moon travels around the Earth. One trip takes about a month. As it moves, we see its sunny side from different angles.

vocabulary.definition: The path something takes as it goes round and round another thing in space.
vocabulary.example: The Moon's orbit goes around the Earth.

pages.image_alt: Earth in the centre, the Moon at several positions on a circle, the Sun far to one side.

pages.text: When the Moon is between us and the Sun, its lit side faces away. We see almost nothing. That is a new moon.
pages.illustration_brief: Diagram position: Moon between Earth and Sun, dark side toward Earth; a tiny dark disc in a corner sky.
pages.audio_script: When the Moon is between us and the Sun, its lit side faces away. We see almost nothing. That is a new moon.
pages.image_alt: The Moon between Earth and Sun, dark side toward Earth; a tiny dark disc in a corner sky.

pages.text: A week later we see half of the lit side. That is a first quarter moon. It looks like a letter D.
pages.illustration_brief: A half-lit Moon, right side bright, like a D.
pages.audio_script: A week later we see half of the lit side. That is a first quarter moon. It looks like a letter D.
pages.image_alt: A half-lit Moon, right side bright, like a D.

pages.text: Another week, and the Moon is on the far side of the Earth from the Sun. Now its whole lit face points at us. Full moon!
pages.illustration_brief: Diagram: Sun, Earth, Moon in a line with the Moon furthest; a big full Moon.
pages.audio_script: Another week, and the Moon is on the far side of the Earth from the Sun. Now its whole lit face points at us. Full moon!
pages.image_alt: Sun, Earth, Moon in a line with the Moon furthest; a big full Moon.

pages.text: Then it shrinks again: half, then a slice, then new moon, and the month starts over. New, half, full, half. Watch for a month and you will see it.
pages.illustration_brief: A row of eight Moon phases from new to full and back, arranged in a gentle arc.
pages.audio_script: Then it shrinks again: half, then a slice, then new moon, and the month starts over. New, half, full, half. Watch for a month and you will see it.
pages.image_alt: A row of Moon phases from new to full and back, arranged in a gentle arc.

quiz.prompt: Where does the Moon's light come from?
quiz.explanation: Page 3: It shines because sunlight bounces off it.

quiz.prompt: Why does the Moon look like it changes shape?

options.text: We see different amounts of its lit side as it moves around Earth

quiz.explanation: Page 2: what changes is how much of it we see lit up. Page 4: as it moves, we see its sunny side from different angles.

quiz.prompt: Which phase comes about a week after new moon?
quiz.explanation: Page 5 is new moon; page 6 says a week later we see half, the first quarter.
Page 3 explains the Moon shines because sunlight bounces off it.

quiz.prompt: Explain to a grown-up why the Moon looks thin some nights, using the torch and ball if you did it.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says the Moon changes; with support: mentions the Sun lighting it, with prompting; independent: Moon is always whole, Sun lights one half, we see more or less of that half as it goes round Earth
quiz.explanation: The misconception that the Moon actually changes shape is the key thing to hear corrected.

activities.prompt: Put the phases in order, starting from new moon.

activities.claim: The Moon is always a whole ball.

off_screen_prompt: Draw the Moon tonight. Draw it again in a week. Compare your two drawings.
